correctness.rationale: Rooted leaves, nonleaf vertices with no leaf child, and distinct parents with at least one leaf child do partition the tree. The root differentiation of the labeled EGF deletes the smallest label, leaving an unordered set of increasing subtrees. Thus e^F counts the default root, u−1 adjusts the singleton, and (v−1)(e^(F−uz)−1) adjusts a nonempty set with no singleton. Differentiating formally gives (2); in particular for B=(1−z)b one has B=1−e^(−z)−z+z²/2. The proposed identity gives (1−z)c=z(B′+b)/2−z³/12. Its derivative using B′=e^(−z)−1+z and a=z(2−z)/(2(1−z)) is ab+e^(−z)(a−z), and the constant is zero. Hence (4) is exact. Since (n−1)! trees are divided by n!, moments multiply the extracted coefficient by n; [z^n]a=1/2 for n≥2 and the correction in (4) contributes −n/12 for n≥3. For the leaf variance the conditional leaf increment is 1 minus Bernoulli(L_n/n), giving V_(n+1)=(1−2/n)V_n+1/4 from V_2=0. Thus V_n=n/12, and subtracting from the partition gives Cov(L_n,Q_n)=0. At n=1,2 leaves are deterministic. At n=4 a star has (L,Q)=(3,1), whereas parents (1,1,2) give (2,2), so orthogonality does not generally imply independence. A fresh exact parent-choice enumerator at /workspace/branches/1393abd7-8492-4aaf-a0c3-e3e688cf0460/record5_fresh_enumeration.py, with record5_enumeration.log in the same directory, checked the partition and all three moments over all 46,233 trees of sizes 2–9; this is corroboration only.

evidence: Holmgren–Janson Lemma 3.14 supplies finite-n covariances for arbitrary fringe tolls supported on sizes k and m, with separate cases n>k+m, k<n≤k+m, and n=k. Mahmoud–Ward have a protected marginal mean and variance bounds; Devroye–Janson give the limiting protected proportion.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The asymptotic and marginal results alone do not give the frozen covariance. Lemma 3.14 applies to every size-k tranche of the protected toll and the size-one leaf toll simultaneously. The only nonstandard within-fringe moment needed by this specialization, E_k[f L_k], is supplied by the exact root law.

evidence: For a tree of size k, the root-law factorial transform gives E[(B_k)_j z^L]=z^j E[z^L_(k−j)] for j≤k−2, with star term z^(k−1) for j=k−1. Setting the root mark to zero gives p_k=Pr(B_k=0)=sum_{j=0}^{k−1} (−1)^j/j!. Differentiating at z=1 uses mean (k+j)/2 for j≤k−2 and k−1 for the star term. The alternating sum gives E[L_k 1{B_k=0}]=(k−1)p_k/2. In Lemma 3.14 set m=1, with g the singleton toll. Equation (1.18) then gives β(k,1)=(k²+2k+2)/(2k(k+1)(k+2)).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Insert those moments in parts (ii)–(iv) of Lemma 3.14 and sum over k=2,…,n. The covariance divided by −n/2 is S_n=sum_{k=2}^{n−2} (k+4)p_k/[k(k+1)(k+2)] + 2p_(n−1)/[(n−1)n] + p_n/n; the last two terms are the exact boundary cases. S_3=1/6. Subtraction gives S_(n+1)−S_n=((p_n−p_(n−1))+n(p_(n+1)−p_n))/[n(n+1)]=0, since consecutive factorial increments cancel. This is the precise all-n covariance −n/12, not only its slope. The leaf variance is already standard, and subtracting it via the partition gives orthogonality. The finite nonindependence example adds no separate mathematical gap once the exact covariance is covered.

Once Var(L_n)=n/12 is known, Cov(L_n,Q_n)=0 and Cov(L_n,P_n)=−n/12 are equivalent by the rooted partition. The covariance with B_n itself is not the frozen covariance.

originality.rationale: No inspected source was found to print exactly this global leaf-parent covariance. However, it is mechanically implied by the indexed exact joint law at the root and Holmgren–Janson's exact finite-size fringe covariance formula, including its endpoint cases. Specialization to singleton fringe counts gives a sum that telescopes using the alternating factorial increments. The conclusion rests on the explicit derivation below, not on the similarity of the root and global observables, or on an asymptotic limit.
residual_risks: The bounded search does not determine historical priority for stating the exact global zero covariance. The ruling uses an explicit implication of prior exact results and does not rely on absence of matches or on the nearby asymptotic results.

value.rationale: The exact orthogonality of two natural dependent counts would be a useful finite-size invariant if not already implied; the short increasing-tree proof is also mathematically sound. But the precise frozen identity follows from the known root transform and the exact fringe covariance lemma by substitution and an elementary factorial telescoping. Neither the equivalent covariance, the known leaf variance, nor the four-vertex witness adds a distinct unknown result.
